title: Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.9
exact_target: Can finitely many open subgroups of a finite-rank nonabelian free pro-$p$ group have no common nontrivial subgroup characteristic in each of them?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Fix a prime $p$. A pro-$p$ group is a topological group that is an
inverse limit of finite $p$-groups, with its compact inverse-limit topology.
Let $F$ be a free pro-$p$ group of finite rank $r\ge2$: it is topologically
generated by $r$ free generators, with the universal mapping property
for continuous maps of those generators into pro-$p$ groups.
The rank restriction makes $F$ nonabelian.

Use the pro-$p$ convention that subgroups under consideration are closed
and automorphisms are continuous. A subgroup $U\le F$ is open when it
is open in this topology; it then has finite index. A subgroup $C\le U$
is characteristic in $U$ if every continuous automorphism of $U$ maps
$C$ onto itself.

Does there exist a finite list of open subgroups $U_1,\ldots,U_m$ of
$F$, including $F$ itself, such that
\[
 \left[C\le\bigcap_{i=1}^m U_i\quad\text{and}\quad
       C\text{ is characteristic in every }U_i\right]
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad C=1
\]
for every closed subgroup $C$ of $F$?

The subgroup $C$ is the same subgroup in all conditions; one is not
intersecting arbitrarily selected characteristic subgroups of different
$U_i$. The chosen list may depend on $F$ and $p$, but must be finite.
The open subgroups need not themselves be characteristic or normal in
$F$. The member $U_i=F$ ensures that a candidate $C$ is also characteristic
in the full free pro-$p$ group.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Can finitely many open subgroups of a finite-rank nonabelian free pro-$p$ group have no common nontrivial subgroup characteristic in each of them?
